question:
A logistics firm has a partnership with two vendors for the delivery of three items X, Y, Z. Given the following matrices for number of deliveries in January ($D_1$) and February ($D_2$):

$D_1 = \begin{bmatrix}60 & 45 & 55 \\ 80 & 60 & 65\end{bmatrix}$

$D_2 = \begin{bmatrix}70 & 50 & 60 \\ 90 & 75 & 80\end{bmatrix}$

Rows: Vendor 1 and Vendor 2. Columns: Items X, Y, Z.

(i) Compute the month-on-month percentage growth delivery matrix.

(ii) If in March, each vendor delivers items such that deliveries form an identity matrix (explain your answer and why or why not this is possible).

(iii) For February, what is the scalar multiplication needed to make the maximum value of $D_2$ equal to 100?

(iv) Is $D_2$ a diagonal, scalar, or identity matrix? Justify.

(v) Find $D_2'$ and state the relation between $D_2'$ and $D_2$ regarding symmetry.
explanation:
(i) Percentage growth: $\frac{D_2 - D_1}{D_1} \times 100$

First row: $(70-60)/60 \times 100 = 16.67$, $(50-45)/45 \times 100 = 11.11$, $(60-55)/55 \times 100 = 9.09$

Second row: $(90-80)/80 \times 100 = 12.5$, $(75-60)/60 \times 100 = 25$, $(80-65)/65 \times 100 = 23.08$

So, $\begin{bmatrix}16.67 & 11.11 & 9.09 \\ 12.5 & 25 & 23.08\end{bmatrix}$

(ii) Deliveries as identity matrix:

Identity matrix for $2\times2$ is $\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}$; for $D_1$ and $D_2$ ($2\times3$), not possible as identity matrix is only defined for square matrices.

(iii) Maximum of $D_2$ is 90. To make it 100: Multiply by $k$ such that $k\times90=100 \implies k=\frac{100}{90}=1.11$

(iv) $D_2$ is not diagonal (diagonal elements only are not all other elements zero), not scalar (diagonal and equal elements), not identity (ones on diagonal, zero elsewhere). It is a general matrix.

(v) $D_2' = \begin{bmatrix}70 & 90 \\ 50 & 75 \\ 60 & 80\end{bmatrix}$. $D_2$ is not square, so cannot be symmetric or skew-symmetric.

options.A:
(i) Growth matrix $=\begin{bmatrix}10&5&5\\10&15&15\end{bmatrix}$.
(ii) Identity matrix is possible because $D_2$ has two rows.
(iii) Scalar multiplier is $100$.
(iv) $D_2$ is an identity matrix.
(v) $D_2'=D_2$, so it is symmetric.
options.B:
(i) Growth matrix $=\begin{bmatrix}16.67&11.11&9.09\\12.5&25&23.08\end{bmatrix}$.
(ii) Identity matrix is possible for any rectangular matrix.
(iii) Scalar multiplier is $\frac{90}{100}$.
(iv) $D_2$ is scalar.
(v) $D_2$ is skew-symmetric.
options.C:
(i) Month-on-month percentage growth matrix is approximately $\begin{bmatrix}16.67&11.11&9.09\\12.50&25&23.08\end{bmatrix}$.
(ii) An identity matrix is not possible here because the delivery matrix is $2\times3$, while identity matrices are square.
(iii) Required scalar multiplier is $\frac{100}{90}=\frac{10}{9}\approx1.11$.
(iv) $D_2$ is neither diagonal, scalar, nor identity; it is a general rectangular matrix.
(v) $D_2'=\begin{bmatrix}70&90\\50&75\\60&80\end{bmatrix}$, and since $D_2$ is not square, it cannot be symmetric or skew-symmetric.
options.D:
(i) Percentage growth matrix is zero.
(ii) Identity matrix is possible only if all entries are $1$.
(iii) Scalar multiplier is $9$.
(iv) $D_2$ is diagonal.
(v) $D_2'$ is not defined.
